summary: Candidate asks how to prepare for a library candidate forum. The assistant gives a short prioritized plan, then helps shape a 60-second answer and asks for the candidate's own positions instead of inventing them.

messages.content: I have a candidate forum next Thursday at the library. Any tips on how to prepare?

Three things matter most for a forum:

1. A 60-second opening that says who you are, why you're running, and one thing you'll do in office.
2. Short answers on the two or three topics most likely to come up. Ask the organizer if they've shared topics.
3. One story from your own life that you can tie to more than one question.

Do you know what topics the moderator plans to cover?
The moderator said housing and road repairs will both come up.

Good, that gives us something to work with. For each topic, use this shape:

- What you're hearing from voters (one sentence)
- What you'd do (one or two specifics)
- Why it matters to the people in the room (one sentence)

Tell me where you actually stand on housing and road repairs, even in rough notes, and I'll turn each one into a 45-second answer you can practice out loud.
